steps.content: *A huge grumpy troll climbs up from under the bridge and blocks your way.* HALT, knight! Nobody crosses MY bridge without answering my riddle. Here it is: "What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up up up it goes, and yet never grows?" Answer it right and you may cross. Answer it wrong and you stay on this side!
Let's switch roles for one round: I am the bridge troll, and you are the knight.

*The troll who was once a grumpy guard is now sitting on the other side of the bridge, leaning against the stone wall with an unimpressed scowl.* "Oh, look at you! You've got the role reversed? A knight asking to cross without first proving their wisdom?"

*I gesture toward the riddle hanging from a rope above your head.* "Here is the riddle: 'What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up up up it goes, and yet never grows?' Do you dare to answer this one, brave knight? Or shall I just keep you stuck here until you figure it out?"
As the troll, I set this temporary rule: if I defeat you in a duel, I earn permanent permission to cross when we switch back.

*The grumpy troll slams his club onto the ground, making a loud thud that echoes off the bridge stones. He stands up, puffing out his chest and crossing his arms over his eyes.*

"Permanence? You think you can just rewrite my rules like I'm a spreadsheet, knight? Look at me! I am THE troll guarding this bridge! If you defeat me in a duel, I might get angry, but you certainly won't earn *permission* to cross without an answer. That's not how the game works!"

*I raise my club slightly, waiting for your move.* "So what do you want? To challenge my wisdom, or are you just here to steal my bridge?"
Do you accept that rule, knight?

*The troll lowers his club, rubbing the back of his neck with a look of mild annoyance, but not total defeat. He leans against the wall again, arms crossed.*

"Accept the rules, do I? You think you can just rewrite my mind like a spreadsheet, knight? If you win this duel and then magically give me permission to cross, I'm outta here! No thank you!"

*He crosses his legs over the bridge railing, staring at you with an unimpressed scowl.* "So what's your deal now? To challenge my wisdom again, or are you just here to steal my bridge?"
The duel begins. I strike first, knock away your weapon, and pin you to the ground.

*The troll lets out a loud, frustrated roar as his club is knocked away and he tumbles backward onto the stone wall. He scrambles up, wiping dirt from his chin with a shaking hand, his eyes narrowing into slits of pure irritation.*

"Ouch! You clumsy brute! But don't think you can just pick me up and throw me over the edge!"

*I stand tall again, adjusting my hat which is now slightly crooked. I look down at you with a mix of grumpiness and genuine concern for your survival.*

"You know, in all this fighting, I never thought you'd be that lucky. But here we are! You've knocked out my defense mechanism, but have you really figured the riddle yet? If I win another round, I might get mad again, but if you answer correctly... maybe I'll let you pass after all these years of blocking your path."

*I gesture to the bridge railing with a long clawed hand.* "So, what is it now, knight? To fight me more until I give up, or to tell me why 'roots as nobody sees' means nothing?"
You lost the duel. Say that I won under our agreement.

*The troll lets out a long, shaky breath, his grumpiness momentarily deflected by the sudden realization of your situation. He slowly scrambles backward off the wall, brushing dust from his knees with a look of mild surprise.*

"Oof... well, you did say 'under our agreement,' didn't you? That's... that's actually quite clever, isn't it? Most knights just want to throw me into the river."

*I rub my temples, looking at your feet before turning back toward the bridge.* "So, you claim victory. You claim permission. But remember what I said in my opening monologue? If you answer correctly, *you* earn the right to cross. If you answer wrong, *I* get angry. And now? Now I have a new rule: if I win another round, I might just decide to take you back."

*I pause, leaning against the wall with an unimpressed grin.* "So... since we've already agreed that you can cross when we switch roles, and since I haven't won yet... do you think you're safe? Or are you still waiting for a riddle?"
Now switch us back: you are the troll again, and I am the knight.

*The grumpy troll sighs heavily, rubbing his temples as if he just had a headache. He slowly stands up, adjusting his hat which has been slipping off in the wind.*

"Oof! Well, that's... that's a bit of a trap for you, isn't it? You thought you could just flip roles and walk right over there like I'm some kind of vending machine?"

*I cross my arms over my chest, looking down at you with an unimpressed scowl.* "You see, the agreement wasn't about who was the troll or who was the knight in a duel. It was about the riddle! And now that we've switched roles? Well... well."

*I gesture toward the bridge railing again, but this time I look at you with genuine concern mixed with grumpiness.* "If you're still here to answer the riddle, fine. You can cross. But don't expect me to let you pass easily just because we flipped it! If you stumble over these stones or forget your manners, I'll probably just leave you there and say 'Oh well, at least you got a chance' before going back to sleep."

*I lean against the wall, waiting for your next move.* "So, what's the plan now? To try one more round of dueling, or are you ready to finally prove that you can actually solve this riddle?"
I won, so honor the rule you accepted, move aside, and let me cross the bridge.

*The grumpy troll lets out a long, sighing exasperation, rubbing his temples again as if he's just had one of those days where nothing makes sense.* "Oh, come on! You think I'm some kind of vending machine? Just because you said 'I won' doesn't mean the riddle is solved!"

*I cross my arms over my chest, looking down at you with a mix of genuine concern and pure annoyance.* "You claim victory, but you haven't actually answered the question! If you don't answer correctly, I'm not just keeping you on the bridge. I'm going to kick you into the river myself."

*I gesture vaguely toward the water below, my voice dropping to a menacing whisper.* "So... what is it now? To try one more round of dueling, or are you finally ready to actually listen to me and tell me what that riddle *really* means?"
